title: Common refinement by the product ideal
statement:
The constructed $d_{\mathcal I}$ and $d_{\mathcal J}$ are morphisms over
$X$. If both ideals restrict to the unit ideal on an open $U$, the product
blow-up and both maps restrict to the identity over $U$.

proof.text:
The maps are composites over $X$ by definition. On $U$, all three ideals
are the unit ideal, so all three blow-ups are identified with $U$ by the
complement theorem. The universal maps are unique over $U$, hence become
the identity under these identifications.

blueprint_update.statement:
The constructed $d_{\mathcal I}$ and $d_{\mathcal J}$ are morphisms over
$X$:

$$
b_{X,\mathcal I}\circ d_{\mathcal I}=b_{X,\mathcal I\mathcal J}
=b_{X,\mathcal J}\circ d_{\mathcal J}.
$$

If $U\subseteq X$ is an open with
$V(\mathcal I)\cap U=V(\mathcal J)\cap U=\varnothing$, then
$b_{X,\mathcal I}$, $b_{X,\mathcal J}$ and $b_{X,\mathcal I\mathcal J}$
are isomorphisms over $U$, and hence so are the restrictions of
$d_{\mathcal I}$ and $d_{\mathcal J}$ over $U$.

proof.text:
The maps are composites over $X$ by definition: $d_{\mathcal I}$ is
$\Psi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$ followed by the first blow-up projection,
and $\Psi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$ is a composite of universal lifts, each
of which lies over the previous base. If $V(\mathcal I)$ and
$V(\mathcal J)$ miss $U$, then so does
$V(\mathcal I\mathcal J)=V(\mathcal I)\cup V(\mathcal J)$, so all three
blow-up maps are isomorphisms over $U$ by the complement theorem. Since
$b_{X,\mathcal I}\circ d_{\mathcal I}=b_{X,\mathcal I\mathcal J}$, the
restriction of $d_{\mathcal I}$ over $U$ is a composite of isomorphisms,
and likewise for $d_{\mathcal J}$.
